arxiv-1510-01234.title: Hardware Random number Generator for cryptography
arxiv-1510-01234.creator: Ram Soorat, Madhuri K. and Ashok Vudayagiri
arxiv-1510-01234.description: Abstract One of the key requirement of many schemes is that of random numbers. Sequence of random numbers are used at several stages of a standard cryptographic protocol. A simple example is of a Vernam cipher, where a string of random numbers is added to massage string to generate the encrypted code.

arxiv-1907-12955.title: Latest results from the NA62 experiment at CERN
arxiv-1907-12955.description: Abstract NA62 is a fixed target kaon experiment at the CERN SPS which aims at measuring the branching ratio of the K + → π + ​ ν ​ ν ¯ K^{+}\to\pi^{+}\nu\bar{\nu} decay with 10 % 10\text{\,}\% precision. This ultra-rare kaon decay is theoretically extremely clean and an ideal place to look for physics beyond the Standard Model.

arxiv-2006-05275.title: On the complexity of the universality and inclusion problems for unambiguous context-free grammars (Invited Paper) Thanks: This work has been partially supported by the Polish NCN grant 2017/26/D/ST6/00201. This is a technical report of an invited paper of the same title to appear in the proceedings
arxiv-2006-05275.creator: Lorenzo Clemente
arxiv-2006-05275.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Lorenzo Clemente. We study the computational complexity of universality and inclusion problems for unambiguous finite automata and context-free grammars. We observe that several such problems can be reduced to the universality problem for unambiguous context-free grammars. The latter problem has long been known to be decidable and we propose a PSPACE algorithm that works by reduction to the zeroness problem of recurrence equations with convolution. We are not aware of any non-trivial complexity lower bounds.

arxiv-2309-08904.creator: Xiang Zhu*, Zixuan Chen*, Jianyu Chen
arxiv-2309-08904.description: Abstract In recent years, Reinforcement Learning (RL) is becoming a popular technique for training controllers for robots. For example, people learn table tennis skills by imitating the motions of coaches.

arxiv-2505-14161.title: Personalized Bayesian Federated Learning with Wasserstein Barycenter Aggregation
arxiv-2505-14161.creator: Ting Wei, Biao Mei, Junliang Lyu, Renquan Zhang, Feng Zhou, Yifan Sun
arxiv-2505-14161.description: Abstract Personalized Bayesian federated learning (PBFL) handles non-i.i.d. client data and quantifies uncertainty by combining personalization with Bayesian inference. However, existing PBFL methods face two limitations: restrictive parametric assumptions in client posterior inference and naive parameter averaging for server aggregation. To overcome these issues, we propose FedWBA, a novel PBFL method that enhances both local inference and global aggregation.

arxiv-2506-06666.creator: Oktay Karakuş, Hasan Arkadaş
arxiv-2506-06666.description: Abstract Line-breaking passes (LBPs) are crucial tactical actions in football, allowing teams to penetrate defensive lines and access high-value spaces. pmc-13048277.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Mental disorders refer to abnormal states that affect an individual’s thinking, emotion, behavior, and perception, and are generally associated with dysregulation of brain function. They exhibit genetic heterogeneity as well as multi-level structural and functional abnormalities of the brain. uslaw-usc-t41-s1301.title: 41 U.S.C. § 1301 — Definition
uslaw-usc-t41-s1301.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t41-s1301.description: United States Code, Title 41 (Public Contracts); Chapter 13 (Acquisition Councils); Subchapter I (Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. In this subchapter, the term “Council” means the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council established under section 1302(a) of this title.
